Yes. 

The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. Throughout the story, the central tension is the unspoken romantic connection between Ines and Marta, heavily symbolized by two recurring motifs: Marta's lit window at night (which Ines initially views as "a lit thing she was not invited into") and the tide chart with its circled "window" of time. 

The conclusion brings both of these motifs to a satisfying resolution. After finally confessing their mutual feelings and carving out four extra days to be together, Ines turns on her own bedroom lamp to answer Marta's light across the courtyard. By ending with the two women looking at each other through their lit windows and referencing the tide chart one last time, the writer arrives at the exact emotional and thematic moment the entire piece was building toward, offering a complete and resonant sense of closure.
